title: The factory-circuit write-ups
ask: Should the thirteen factory-circuit write-ups be parsed into rows and the files dropped, or stay as the one prose the car folder keeps?
why: The thirteen factory-circuit write-ups in the reference (one Markdown page per factory circuit, from the 1982 wiring diagram) are what the Manual's Diagrams page shows today, grouped by system through the circuits table. They are prose, and D-519 says the car's truth is tables, not documents - so either they are parsed into rows (one table of each circuit's path: the parts it passes, the wire colours, the fuse, the grounds, with the page rendering that) and the files go, or they stay as the one kind of prose the car folder keeps, beside 00-CAR/data/procedures. How the Manual reads is yours.
options:
(a) Parse them into rows: a circuit_paths table (circuit, step order, part, terminal, wire colour, fuse, ground, note) that the Diagrams page renders as the write-up read today; the Markdown files leave the tree; the wiring-diagram PDF stays in the ignored library as the source. A day of agent work; nothing lost that a row cannot say.
(b) Keep the write-ups as files under 00-CAR (a circuits folder beside procedures), the circuits table pointing at them; the Diagrams page unchanged. Nothing to do now; the one prose exception stays.
(c) Both: the rows for the app and the page, the files kept as the long-form reading until the rows prove enough, then dropped.
recommend: (a), unless you read them as pages often - then (c) until the rows prove enough.
stops: T3 (the rename) and the write-ups' move; T1 and T2 proceed.

title: How deep the manuals are parsed
ask: How deep is each manual parsed before its file leaves the tree: what the Manual shows, every page as rows, or only the device manuals for now?
why: The intake holds about forty documents with files: the 1985 workshop manual by section, the 1980 technical data, the parts catalogue microfiche, the training manual, the emissions guide, bulletins and brochures, plus the device manuals the projects use. D-519 says each is parsed into the car's tables and taken out of the tree. How deep decides the work: the figures and procedures the Manual shows (specs, intervals, procedures, terminals, the catalogue rows already transcribed) is weeks of agent runs from the Plan button; every page of every manual as rows is months, most of it never shown. The research tooling already did wave 1 (terminals, parts, specs); the depth is yours.
options:
(a) What the Manual shows: every spec, interval, torque, capacity, procedure step and terminal the car's tables have columns for, from every section; the rest of a page is not transcribed. Weeks of runs; the files leave the tree as each section is done.
(b) As (a), plus the full text of each section as searchable rows (a page table: source, page, heading, text) so nothing in a manual is lost when its file goes. Roughly double the runs; the record grows by tens of thousands of rows.
(c) The device manuals and the catalogue only for now (the projects need them); the workshop manual sections stay in the tree until the strip reaches each system. Least now; the reference keeps its PDFs for months.
recommend: (a), unless you want every word kept searchable in the app - then (b).
stops: The parse rows T4 seeds (they are added gated on this block); the moves T1-T3 proceed.

title: What the public repository may carry
ask: Should the repository go private, or stay public with the copyrighted manuals moved out of git, and what licence does its own code carry?
why:
The repository github.com/CamdenThomas/Rx7 is public, and it carries about 240 MB of PDFs that are not ours to give away: the Mazda workshop manual sections, the 1982 wiring diagram scan, the parts catalogue, ECUMaster's PMU manual and the TE connector catalogue (sources S-001, S-002, S-005, S-007 - whose own note says 'Mazda copyright, private use'). The free CAD library and the bought 3D model were kept out of git for exactly that reason (D-418); the manuals were not. The same public repository carries your name, your town's junkyards and your words in every decision. The phone reads the record from GitHub without a key today because the repository is public; the fine-grained token it already uses to write reads a private one just as well. A public repository that bundles OFL fonts, MPL Pyodide and MIT code should also say what licence its own code and text are under (02-APP/app/THIRD-PARTY.md lists what is bundled); each option below names the licence choice it comes with, and you can change that part in words. Redistributing others' manuals and choosing a licence are yours to decide.

Re-raised here from REF.01 on 2026-10-13 (D-519): the reference stops being an area, so its block moves with the intake's work. The reference's bulk is leaving git either way (T2); what remains to decide is below.
options:
(a) Make the repository private, and state 'all rights reserved' in a LICENSE file. The manuals stay where they are, the phone keeps working through its token (the token becomes required for reading too), CI keeps running, nothing is rewritten. Nobody outside sees the record; a sponsor showcase would need a separate public face later.
(b) Keep it public, move the manuals and vendor PDFs out of the tree going forward into 01-INTAKE/model/library/docs/ (already gitignored) with fetch.sh re-fetching the public ones and sources.local_path pointing there, and add a LICENSE (MIT for the tool and app code; the record's text all rights reserved). The past commits still hold the PDFs unless the history is rewritten - a force-push CLAUDE.md forbids without your word; say if you want that too.
(c) Keep it public and leave the manuals in, with no LICENSE file: accept the exposure and leave the licence unstated. Cheapest today.
recommend: (a), unless you want the record readable by anyone for the showcase - then (b), and a history rewrite only if you say so.
stops: Plan steps P51 and P52 (a LICENSE file and moving the manuals); nothing in the build.
